current_answer: Current evidence supports several distinct routes: fal H3 Max Director is a finite hosted context-carrying WebRTC session; Yoroll says H3 Superfast powers YoLive, a group proposal-and-vote route; Reactor FastH3 is a high-end queue-and-playout route; FastVideo documents local FastH3 clip paths and a four-GPU Dreamverse frame-carried Preview v1 profile; a community project reports one RTX 5090 sustaining a retimed dense FastH3 channel; Comfy offers local H3 paths; and vLLM-Omni documents a separate H3 service. The new lower-GPU vLLM-Omni record is a single 50-step full-H3 T2VA validation on two RTX 5090 GPUs: 124 frames at 1344×768 / 24 fps, about 5.17 seconds of output, returned in 8 minutes 38 seconds of client end-to-end time. The documented two-GPU DLO route requires at least 200 GiB host RAM, with 384 GiB recommended. It establishes an offline capacity path, not a warm low-latency, live, or transition route. Keep it separate from vLLM-Omni’s dedicated warmed eight-B300 FastH3 T2VA result, which returned a complete 10.125-second MP4 in 8.678 and 8.710 seconds, and from FastH3 8-Step V2’s unresolved ComfyUI FL2VA scope conflict.

catalogue_card.question: Can full H3 run on two RTX 5090s?
catalogue_card.text: vLLM-Omni says one 50-step T2VA job did: 5.17 seconds of 1344×768 / 24 fps output returned in 8 minutes 38 seconds. It needs a large-RAM host and is an offline capacity result, not live video.

summary: vLLM-Omni says one 50-step full-H3 T2VA request completed on two RTX 5090 GPUs: 124 1344×768 frames at 24 fps, about 5.17 seconds of media, in 8 minutes 38 seconds of client end-to-end time.
The current two-GPU DLO recipe requires at least 200 GiB available host RAM and recommends 384 GiB. It reports a valid H.264/AAC output and a sampled per-GPU peak, not a general 5090 benchmark.

This is a single T2VA capacity validation, not a warmed latency test. It does not establish FL2VA/Ref2VA, first visible frame, streaming, queue capacity, cost, quality, retries, continuity, or interactive response.
A separate warmed eight-B300 FastH3 T2VA report returned a complete 10.125-second MP4 in 8.678–8.710 seconds. Do not merge that faster complete-response condition with the two-5090 full-H3 row.
uncertainty: vLLM-Omni’s two-RTX-5090 result is one project-published T2VA validation. The pool did not run it or independently audit its environment, media, timing, or quality.

The reported 8 minutes 38 seconds is client end-to-end for one run, not a warmed multi-run result. It does not establish first frame, streaming, queue, concurrent requests, retries, uptime, cost, or viewer-visible latency.
The two-5090 target validation does not establish FL2VA or Ref2VA. vLLM-Omni’s eight-B300 FastH3 result is a different, warmed dedicated T2VA profile.
Dreamverse’s FastH3 profile is project documentation; the pool did not install or run it, inspect a generated handoff, or measure buffer, cost, recovery, or uptime.
FastVideo and ComfyUI still conflict on FastH3 8-Step V2 FL2VA scope. The pool did not run a pinned T2VA or FL2VA workflow.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end source-to-visible latency measurement, or first-party pool analytics is available.
